text:
Priya: heads up — saw p99 spikes on the latency dashboard for /v1/generate.us-east after we adjusted routing weights this morning. p50 looks flat, p95 up a bit, p99 much worse.
Ben: can you link the slice? I want to see per-endpoint breakdown. sometimes fallback->cpu path causes long tails.
Priya: https://console.redwood/internal/dashboards/latency?endpoint=/v1/generate.us-east — note p50=34ms, p95=78ms, p99=420ms in the 5m window.
Ruth: that's scary. sample_count for that slice is only ~120 in the window. small N amplifies percentile noise.
Omar: are we exposing sample_count in the UI? last I checked only raw percentiles showed.
Priya: no badge today. we only show p50/p95/p99 numbers and a sparkline.
Ben: quick theory: our frontend query calls the rollup API which returns precomputed quantiles from the sampled stream. do we apply sample weights when computing quantiles in the rollup job?
Ruth: I dug into the rollup code last week — it uses t-digest on raw samples, no explicit sample_weight. so quantiles assume uniform sampling.
Omar: that means if sampling probability differs by route or size, quantiles will be biased. fallback routing likely changed distribution.
Priya: propose immediate UX mitigations: (1) surface sample_count next to each percentile, (2) add a tiny "sampled" pill when the source is sampled, (3) annotate timeline where routing policy changed so users can correlate.
Ben: good. low-risk. also run a one-off job to compute weighted quantiles (using sample_weight) for that 5m window so we can compare.
Ruth: small SQL we can run: ```SELECT endpoint, approx_weighted_quantile(0.99, latency_ms, sample_weight) as p99_w, approx_quantile(0.99, latency_ms) as p99_unw, sum(sample_weight) as total_weight, count() as sample_count FROM latency_sampled WHERE endpoint='/v1/generate.us-east' AND time > now()-interval '5 minutes' GROUP BY endpoint;``` should show difference.
Omar: I'll run it in staging and paste results. if weighted p99 drops a lot it's evidence sampling bias.
Deploy Bot: frontend/console-ui v3.2.1 canary deployment started by Ben :rocket:
QA Bot: regression check queued for console-ui v3.2.1 — runs in ~8m
Ben: also a backend contract question: if we keep returning unweighted percentiles, should the frontend label them "sampled-quantile" and link to docs explaining bias?
Priya: yes, transparency first. prefer label + tooltip while we decide on backend semantics.
Ruth: long-term: we should either (A) compute weighted quantiles in rollups, or (B) always use full-traffic aggregations for percentiles at dashboard granularity, or (C) show both (sampled vs full) where feasible.
Omar: engineering cost estimate: weighted-tdigest change is moderate; full-traffic rollups are costly. showing both maybe expensive storage-wise.
Priya: for now: quick triage plan — Omar runs weighted job and posts diffs, Ben lands sample_count badge+tooltip in canary, add routing-change annotation to timeline (product tracker #PLT-824). We'll reconvene after results.
Ben: landing badge now, will update PR link shortly.
Omar: pasted weighted run results: p99_unw=420ms, p99_w=85ms, sample_count=118, total_weight=1245. looks like weighted p99 aligns with p95-ish. I'll attach raw query output to the ticket.
Priya: huge win — confirms sampling-weight bias. ok next steps: Ruth, estimate effort to change rollup to weighted tdigest and potential storage impact. Ben, keep the badge + sampled pill; push annotation UX.
Ruth: will do. estimate 3-4 days for safe rollout with tests.
Priya: thanks folks. adding followups: add doc blurb for console about "percentile provenance" and link to infra ticket.
Ben: noted. PR: https://git.redwood/p/console-ui/changes/2134
Omar: attaching the raw CSV from the weighted run in the ticket.
Priya: closing loop — we'll watch canary and update channel tomorrow AM. :white_check_mark:
